trigger: Stage A pilot — validating the segment/availability model before scaling

SEGMENT_MODEL_VALIDATED.my_model: split each security series into contiguous COMPLETE runs; state resets at every UNOBSERVED_CONTAMINATED bar
SEGMENT_MODEL_VALIDATED.agreement: EXACT on the pilot security — 4,490 segments, median length 2, max 63, identical to my computation
SEGMENT_MODEL_VALIDATED.conclusion: the availability model I intended for Stage A matches the already-registered Massive semantics; no new convention is being invented

PILOT_SECURITY.note: all 15,309 COMPLETE bars are INITIALIZATION_SENSITIVE for EMA200 because no run reaches 200 bars

COVERAGE_IS_STRONGLY_BIMODAL.reading: the universe is not uniformly covered. Some securities are near-continuous (EMA200 valid on 99.4% of bars) while 174 of 476 have literally zero valid EMA200 bars. The aggregate 20.81% is a mixture of two very different populations, not a typical security.

EFFECTIVE_UNIVERSE_BY_DEPTH.definition: securities with more than 20% valid bars for the required EMA depth
EFFECTIVE_UNIVERSE_BY_DEPTH.IMPLICATION: the effective universe SHRINKS WITH FEATURE DEPTH. A P66/D66 token does not operate on 476 securities; it operates on roughly 146. Support floors and multiplicity must be computed against the depth-specific universe, not the nominal 476.

WHY_THIS_MATTERS_MORE_THAN_THE_AGGREGATE: a family-wide "20.81% availability" reads as a uniform thinning. It is not. It is 146 usable securities plus 330 mostly-unusable ones, and that difference changes support floors, clustering, and the independence assumptions behind any multiplicity correction.
STAGE_A_UNAFFECTED: Stage A features (Z, vol, suffix, body_wick, g*, tz_flip, vbo_up) do not depend on deep EMA state and are not governed by this finding
not_done: per-security coverage not yet cross-tabulated against the opening-hour window
